#2444. Galatasaray boss acknowledges summer interest in Stuttgart duo

Bilal El Khannouss was linked with a move away from VfB Stuttgart over the summer, but ultimately stayed with the Bundesliga club.

Speaking to Kicker, Galatasaray director of development Fatih Demireli has now confirmed that the Turkish giants explored a move for the attacking midfielder.

“We had good discussions with him, with VfB Stuttgart and with those around him, but at some point decisions have to be made when it comes to transfers. In the end, we signed Aleksey Batrakov and are very pleased with his development. He has enormous potential, and we want to support him in the best possible way as he continues his journey," he said.

El Khannouss was not the only VfB Stuttgart player to attract interest from Galatasaray, as Ermedin Demirovic was also on their radar. Like his teammate, however, the striker remained at the Bundesliga club.

“Different opportunities arise over the course of a transfer window. In the end, we consciously opted for other solutions,” Demireli explained, admitting:

“It's true that we were interested. Many factors come into play in discussions like these. We also had to take into account the squad regulations in Turkey and ultimately made decisions that we, as a club, are convinced by.”

Stuttgart travel to Turkey to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

#2443. Opinion: The morality of football

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

#2441. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

#2440. Bosz frustrated as Feyenoord hold PSV to 1-1 draw in Eindhoven

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

#2438. Atletico Madrid vs. Bayern Munich preview: Team news and predicted lineups

After being held to a 2-2 draw by Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga, an injury-hit Bayern Munich side turn their attention to Tuesday's trip to Spain to face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The Bavarians will be eager to return to winning ways in Europe's premier club competition, having drawn 3-3 against Viking FK and 2-2 with Arsenal in their last two Champions League outings. Those results have left them 14th in the league phase table with five points from three games.

However, Bayern face a tough test against Atletico Madrid, who are particularly strong at the Wanda Metropolitano, where they haven't lost since a 0-1 defeat to Celta Vigo in May last season.

A 1-1 Champions League draw against another Bundesliga side – VfB Stuttgart – was followed by domestic wins over Deportivo La Coruna (1-0) and Levante (2-0), giving Diego Simeone's men a positive run of results heading into Tuesday's clash. Atletico currently sit second in La Liga.

The two sides have met six times over the past 10 years, with Bayern winning three games, Atletico claiming two victories and one ending in a draw. Bayern have never beaten Atletico away from home and will be keen to change that on Tuesday.

Atletico Madrid will have to manage without Morten Hjulmand after he was shown a straight red card against Stuttgart. Johnny Cardoso (thigh) and Koke (muscle) are both doubts.

As for Bayern Munich, assistant coach Aaron Danks will continue deputising for head coach Vincent Kompany, who remains absent after collapsing and being diagnosed with meningeal irritation.

The German champions suffered a triple injury blow at the weekend, as Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all forced off during their 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund.

Saibari (ankle) and Gnabry (muscle) are both facing longer spells on the sidelines, but Olise could potentially feature after taking part in Bayern's final training session ahead of the game, albeit with his right knee bandaged.

Manuel Neuer also took part in the session and could return from a foot injury, with Jonas Urbig ready to deputise for the veteran goalkeeper once again if he is not passed fit.

Luis Diaz (muscle), Jamal Musiala (thigh) and Bara Sapoko Ndiaye (appendectomy) remain unavailable.

#2436. Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”

Xavi Hernandez has his first win as Netherlands head coach as a Mexx Meerdink double led Oranje to a 2-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League.

Xavi made two changes from the side that drew with Germany as Mexx Meerdink replaced the injured Brian Brobbey up front while Joey Veerman came in for Quinten Timber.

Netherlands dominated from the start but they were forced into an early change when Cody Gakpo suffered a knock and Ruben van Bommel came on.

After half an hour, Crysencio Summerville was clipped in the box and Meerdink made it 1-0 from the penalty spot. It was almost 2-0 before the break but Denzel Dumfries could not convert when through on goal.

Serbia made a double change at the break with Luka Jovic and Dusan Tadic coming on. A minute into the second half, the change worked as Jovic was given space in the box to net after Netherlands failed to clear the ball.

Netherlands went in search of the lead again but Tijjani Reijnders blazed a huge chance over while Ruben van Bommel hit the post. Meerdink did eventually make it 2-1 with a lovely finish after a quick 1-2 with substitute Guus Til.

There was to be no hattrick for Meerdink as he was brought off and Netherlands played the final ten minutes with Til through the middle.

Serbia pressed for a late equaliser but the Netherlands had a golden chance to make it 3-1 when Til found himself in on goal. He had Summerville and Van Bommel to his left but overhit the pass and the later’s finish was too weak to find the net.

The Netherlands held on for the victory which takes them to the top of the group with a clash against Greece next on Thursday.

#2431. Big wins for PSV and Twente close gap on leaders Feyenoord

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

An injury-hit Netherlands side battled back to draw 2-2 against Greece in the Nations League.

Xavi was forced into changes with Cody Gakpo and Jan Paul van Hecke dropping out of the squad. Tijjani Reijnders and Ryan Gravenberch also dropped to the bench with Quinten Timber, Guus Til, Jurrien Timber and Ruben van Bommel starting.

Greece have been in good form recently and their confidence was clear from the start. They had a goal disallowed for offside before Fotis Ioannidis made it 1-0 after 23 minutes.

The Netherlands offered little going forward and in stoppage time, a bad back pass from Van Bommel led to Giorgos Masouras sliding in a second.

Xavi made a triple change as Gravenberch, Noa Lang and Reijnders came on and they all made a big difference as the Netherlands dominated the second half.

Virgil van Dijk headed one back before Denzel Dumfries had two goals disallowed for offside. Xavi turned to Joshua Zirkzee and debutante Gjivai Zechiel in hope of an equaliser.

The equaliser came in the last minute as Zechiel’s overhead kick dropped into the path of Reijnders who blasted the ball in. Zechiel then came close to a winner but his header was straight at the goalkeeper.

A battling point for the Netherlands, who stay unbeaten under Xavi with a game at home to Serbia to come on Sunday.

#2429. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Manchester City Donnarumma; Lewis, Khusanov, Gvardiol (Reis, 46), Mfuni (Alleyne, 46); Kovacic (N González, 46), Reijnders (Ait-Nouri, 46); Savinho (Braithwaite, 78), Foden (Echeverri, 68), Semenyo (Sangare, 68); Mubama (McAidoo, 46).Substitutes not used Bettinelli, Wint, Chabot, Monga, Mukasa, F. Samba, Heskey, Henderson-Hall, Parker.Booked Khusanov (83).Goal Mubama (14).Inter Milan Martinez (Provedel, 61); Augusto (Marello, 69), Bisseck (Maye, 78), Pavard (Bovio, 69); Dimarco (Bastoni, 46), Mkhitaryan (Zielinski, 46), Stankovic (Topalovic, 60), Barella (Frattesi, 46), Diouf (Henrique, 46); Iddrissou (Mosconi, 46), Esposito (Lavelli, 67).Substitutes not used Di Gennaro, Farronato, Sucic, Bonny, Calhanoglu.Booked Stankovic (55).Goal Pavard (20).

Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

On the front foot 👊 pic.twitter.com/AZC7UXYXrj

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Enzo makes 5️⃣ changes at the beginning of the second half 🔄Watch LIVE on CITY+ https://t.co/rVv0RHMeAC pic.twitter.com/TIrLvBlkN3

Reis and Mcaidoo, Ait-Nouri, Alleyne, and Gonzalez are on for City, with Gviardiol one of the players going off, as is Reijnders.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

14. Wonderful work from Semenyo 👊He beats his man on the left to get to the byline, squares it across goal and Divin converts from close range 🎯🐝 1-0 ⚪️ https://t.co/pCDrkfriLY

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

If there are problems at the club, you can pick up on them here.

Welcome to Liverpool, Andoni Iraola!Row between Curtis Jones, Dominik Szoboszlai and Kostas Tsimikas has exposed the work the Spaniard must do to fix a dressing room where personal interests have taken priority.https://t.co/MosO6iCeLm

The fans are out in force in Hong Kong, where the Premier League continues to dominate attention.

Here’s what the former striker told Manchester City: “I’m looking forward to it. I’m not sure Enzo is going to change that much but some tweaks here and there.

“People talking about it being similar to when [Alex] Ferguson left but I don’t think it’s the same, they didn’t have the same infrastructure. He’s a top manager. He will want to put his own stamp on it.”

The biggest story in football right now is increasingly hard to ignore.

Gianni Infantino’s ludicrous plan was sunk almost as soon as it was announced, then he defended himself with such verve as to make himself look completely isolated and apart from the organisation itself, and now UEFA has said it is calling time.

The governing body says it has lost faith in the Peace Prize inventor, a problem which had been in the post for a while now.

The two London sides are facing off in their own pre-season friendly.

You can follow that live here, and find out which player has been sent off.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

The venue in Hong Kong is decent enough and has started filling out. It’s a jaunty 26 degrees, 92% humidity, and raining too. It’s just like being in London during your worst nightmares, basically.

We’ll see how this continues, and if it does continue, over the coming weeks, but Phil Foden has the nod as captain for Enzo Maresca tonight.

Foden signed a new contract recently but has been well off his consistent best for some time now. Another poor season would put him in the frame for the exit door next summer, so this is a chance.

Captaining the side in Enzo's first match as boss 👍©️ pic.twitter.com/bcvIhwXMas

Here is an examination on how Manchester City’s early, £116 million deal left the rest of the transfer market dealing with the implications.

Anderson is still recovering from his World Cup travails,but he could be key to the season, especially if Rodri does depart for Real Madrid soon.

Inter Milan: Martinez, Augusto, Bisseck, Pavard, Dimarco, Mkhitaryan, Stankovic, Barella, Diouf, Iddrissou, Esposito.

Substitutes: Di Gennaro, Provedel, Farronato, Zielinski, Sucic, Henrique, Bonny, Frattesi, Calhanoglu, Bovio, Mosconi, Lavelli, Marello, Maye, Topalovic, Bastoni.

Team news from Hong Kong is in! 🗞️ pic.twitter.com/mselPxNwXr

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Lewis, Khusanov, Gvardiol, Mfuni, Kovacic, Reijnders, Semenyo, Foden (C), Savinho, Mubama.

Subs: Bettinelli, Wint, Chabot, Nico, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Monga, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Mukasa, Alleyne, Sangare, F. Samba, Heskey, Henderson-Hall, Parker.

Our side to face Inter in Hong Kong 🤝XI | Donnarumma, Lewis, Khusanov, Gvardiol, Mfuni, Kovacic, Reijnders, Semenyo, Foden (C), Savinho, MubamaSUBS | Bettinelli, Wint, Chabot, Nico, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Monga, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Mukasa, Alleyne, Sangare, F. Samba,… pic.twitter.com/tYmjiuMudl

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

The Netherlands came back from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw against Greece in the Nations League. Here is our player ratings for the Netherlands players.

Bart Verbruggen 5.5/10: Wasn’t happy with his defence in the first half. Could have done more for the first goal but did make a good save. Had nothing to do after the break.

Denzel Dumfries 5/10: Struggled in the first half before improving in the second. Had two goals disallowed for offside.

Micky van de Ven 5/10: His pace makes up for the gaps he leaves at times and in the firs half he struggled. Like others he got better in the second but had less to do.

Jurrien Timber 4/10: Looked very much like a player who is not fully fit. Second to everything and gave away fouls in the first half. Was too slow too react for the second goal.

Virgil van Dijk 6/10: Defensively he struggled in the first but his goal got his side back into the game after the break.

Joey Veerman 6.5/10: Always looking to make something happen going forward. Not everything worked but was always available. His corner led to a goal an he almost scored a free kick.

Quinten Timber 4/10: Disastrous display as he gave away foul after foul in the first half. Was rightly hooked at half time.

Guus Til 4/10: Like Timber, he offered nothing in the first half and was rightly taken off. Xavi wanted to give him a chance but he didn’t take it.

Crysencio Summerville 6/10: Was Netherlands only outlet going forward in the first half and is a constant threat on the right hand side.

Ruben van Bommel 4.5/10: Was too static at times and his error led to the second goal. Taken off at the break.

Mexx Meerdink 5/10: Tried but was isolated at times. Had no service in the first half and barely touched the ball in the second.

Noa Lang 7/10: Offered more on the left than Van Bommel as he took the game to the Greek defence. His cross led to the equaliser. Likely to start against Serbia after this display.

Tijjani Reijnders 6.5/10: Came on and scored the equaliser with a good finish. Did a lot more running than Til did and it was much needed energy.

Ryan Gravenberch 6.5/10: Immediately helped the Netherlands midfield gain control back in the second half.

Joshua Zirkzee N/A: Not on the pitch long enough for a review

Gjivai Zechiel N/A: Not on the pitch long enough for a review

FT Greece 2-2 NetherlandsA battling draw after being 2-0 down. Had 2 goals disallowed too! Much better second half but that first half was a disaster

Netherlands edged out Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven to move top of their Nations League group.

Xavi decided to name Teun Koopmeiners in the starting eleven but at centre-back alongside Virgil van Dijk, who was earning his 100th cap. Ryan Gravenberch, Tijjani Reijnders and Noa Lang all came into the eleven.

Netherlands made a strong start and missed two good chances to take the lead within the first two minutes. They then dominated possession but it took until the 31st minute for Oranje to take the lead. Koopmeiners free kick evaded everyone and nestled in the corner.

Oranje were only ahead for four minutes as Mihaijo Cvetkovic was allowed far too much space in the Netherlands box to loop in a header. It could have been worse for the Netherlands before the break but Pavlovic squandered a chance when in on goal.

Xavi brought on Joshua Zirkzee for Mexx Meerdink at the break but the best chances early in the second half were for Serbia. Cvetkovic should have put the visitors ahead.

Xavi turned to the bench again with Gjivai Zechiel, Ruben van Bommel and Jorrel Hato all appearing. Reijnders should have made it 2-1 but when through on goal he scooped the ball over the bar.

Netherlands retook the lead after 72 minutes with Denzel Dumfries crossing for Reijnders to square it to an unmarked Zirkzee, who tapped in. It should have been 3-1 straight away but Reijnders was denied through on goal.

The Netherlands sat back and that allowed Serbia to put on pressure. That pressure increased when Micky van de Ven was forced off and Oranje played the last five minutes with only ten men.

Bart Verbruggen made a big save to deny Nemanja Gudelj and Netherlands managed to hold on for the three points.

Netherlands first four games under Xavi see them win two and draw two. They will finish the Nations League at home to Germany and then away to Greece.

FT Netherlands 2-1 SerbiaIt’s three points but far from convincing in the end. Xavi remains unbeaten in his first four games in charge

#2424. Bayern boss gives fresh injury update on Olise and Neuer ahead of Atletico Madrid trip

Despite Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer both taking part in Bayern Munich's final training session ahead of Tuesday's Champions League away clash against Atletico Madrid, it remains unclear whether – and to what extent – either player will feature.

Olise, who was forced off in the second half of Saturday's 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund, trained with his knee bandaged on Monday. Meanwhile, Neuer returned to team training after missing the previous three games due to a foot problem.

Speaking on Monday, Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl provided an update on the duo's fitness.

“As for Michael Olise, we’ll take another look at him tomorrow; we’re taking it day by day," Eberl said.

“It’s good that he’s travelling with us, because he’s an outstanding player who’s always a great asset. However, we’ll avoid the risk of it turning into a long-term injury. Manuel Neuer has been out for quite some time but has been training, so we’ll see how it goes,” he added.

Eberl also stressed Bayern's determination to return to winning ways in the Champions League after drawing their last two games in the competition, while acknowledging how difficult it is to come away with a positive result on the road against Atletico Madrid.

“It’s a top Champions League fixture. We need to show resilience right now. We must keep going if we want to win major titles, and that’s what we want. We want to win in Madrid. The points we dropped in Stavanger are still hanging over us; tomorrow we have a chance to make amends," he said.

“It’s definitely one of the trickiest away fixtures you can face in the Champions League, against opponents who are extremely tough to play against and possess a very high standard of quality, where we’ll have to bring to the game the resilience we’ve had to demonstrate over the past few weeks. They're a team who really will demand everything of us. We’re always under pressure, but we're still heading there to try to achieve the best possible result.”

#2418. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

Man Utd: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c)(Armer 73), Heaven, Shaw (Amass 73); Santos (Thwaites 82), Mount; Amad (J. Fletcher 46), Lacey (Zirkzee 73), Dorgu (Williams 73); Mbeumo (Gabriel 82).Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Kamason, T. FletcherBooked: Heaven (50)Goals: Mbeumo (53 pen, 74)Atletico: Oblak (Esquivel 46), Domínguez (Boñar 61), Le Normand (Giménez 46), Hancko (D. Martínez 61), Ruggeri (Romeo 61), Koke (Hjulmand 46), Obed Vargas (Mendoza 46), Castillo (Iker Luque 61), Arnau Ortiz (Sergio Esteban 61), Carlos Martín (Lemar 61), Lookman (Solà 61)Goals: Arnau Ortiz (5)

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

OFF: Shaw, Dorgu, Lacey, MaguireON: Armer, Amass, Zirkzee, Williams

Big save from Heaton to deny Atletico at the near post after Yoro was beaten by a lovely pass from Lemar.

The energy and intensity of the first half has largely disappeared in this half. Neither keeper has been worked.

OFF: Domínguez, Hancko, Ruggeri, Arnau, Castillo, Carlos Martín, Lookman.ON: Boñar, Solà, D. Martínez, Lemar, Romeo, Iker Luque, Sergio Esteban.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.

OFF: Oblak, Le Normand, Koke, Obed VargasON: Esquivel, Giménez, Mendoza, Hjulmand

J. Fletcher coming for United in place of Amad.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#2416. INTERVIEW: Philipp Lahm senses Harry Kane would trade Ballon d'Or for Champions League glory

MÜNCHEN (Bulinews) Former Bayern Munich star Philipp Lahm, speaking at a media round attended by Bulinews.com, was delighted with Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph but feels the striker would trade it in for top honours in Europe.

“It’s a personal award. I think [winning it] is more important for the offensive players rather than the rest. So, [someone like ex-Bayern star] Franck Ribery will be happy Kane won the Ballon d’Or.

“We all know how important the FC Bayern team is for Kane’s success too. Since I never had the chance to win this award, as a captain I think more of the team as a whole.

“I think Harry Kane would exchange his Ballon d’Or for a Champions League title. Most players grew up playing as a team from a very young age,” Lahm explained, alluding to the collective aspect of football teams.

Interestingly, the 2014 World Cup winner went on to explain why he feels it is difficult to win the Ballon d’Or as a German playing in the domestic top-flight. His theory is largely linked to external noise and catching the public eye.

“As for Kane and Michael Olise [ranked 9th in the Ballon d’Or], they came from another country. I think it’s quite difficult for a German player playing in the Bundesliga to win this award. Think of Florian Wirtz for example.

“It’s all about the attention. When you are successful with the German national team then you become visible. Then when you play successful football for a club like Liverpool, the attention in the UK is much bigger.

“That’s important for this award. It [less attention] makes it more difficult for a player to win it in the Bundesliga rather than changing to another league [and club]. But I do hope the best players stay in the Bundesliga.

“I hope with players like Harry Kane that a lot of other players will follow now it’s possible to win [the Ballon d’Or playing in the Bundesliga],” Lahm concluded, underlining his hope that others may be inspired by the Englishman.

#2415. Bayern Munich : Excellente nouvelle pour Vincent Kompany !

Hospitalisé d'urgence en fin de semaine dernière, Vincent Kompany a pu regagner son domicile ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026. L'entraîneur belge du Bayern Munich va désormais poursuivre sa convalescence au calme, avant d'envisager son retour.

Vincent Kompany avait été hospitalisé d'urgence le vendredi 23 octobre 2026 après avoir été victime d'un malaise au centre d'entraînement de la Säbener Straße, alors qu'il observait une séance de l'équipe réserve du Bayern Munich. Rapidement pris en charge par les services médicaux, le technicien belge a passé plusieurs jours sous observation à l'hôpital. Sur la chaîne allemande ARD, le directeur sportif munichois Max Eberl a d'ailleurs officialisé la cause de cet incident : ce malaise était consécutif à une méningite, soit une inflammation des méninges apparue après un épisode viral. Une alerte sérieuse désormais sous contrôle.

Autorisé à quitter l'hôpital ce mercredi pour poursuivre sa convalescence et son traitement médical à son domicile, Vincent Kompany entame donc une phase de repos indispensable. Selon les informations du journaliste Fabrizio Romano, le Bayern Munich souhaite absolument que son entraîneur se repose et soit à 100 % de sa forme avant d'envisager son retour sur le banc de touche. Aucune prise de risque inutile ne sera tolérée par l'état-major allemand. D'ailleurs, l'entraîneur adjoint Aaron Danks a indiqué qu'aucune date précise de reprise n'était fixée, confirmant que le club bavarois entendait lui laisser tout le temps nécessaire pour récupérer pleinement.

Pendant cette période délicate, le staff bavarois a su parfaitement assurer la continuité sur les terrains. En effet, l'intérim assuré par Aaron Danks s'est soldé par deux victoires probantes en l'espace de quelques jours. Dimanche 25 octobre 2026, les Munichois sont allés s'imposer sur la pelouse du SC Fribourg (3-1) en Bundesliga, avant de signer un large succès face au FC Magdebourg (6-1) le mercredi 28 octobre, à l'occasion du deuxième tour de la Coupe d'Allemagne. Une dynamique sportive rassurante avant un grand rendez-vous national, puisque le Bayern Munich recevra le Borussia Dortmund à l'Allianz Arena le samedi 31 octobre 2026 à 18h30, dans le cadre de la 8e journée de Bundesliga.

#2414. « Ce n'est même pas moi qui prends la décision, c'est le neurochirurgien » : Arthur Desmas forcé d'arrêter sa carrière à 32 ans

Invité sur le plateau du Late Football Club sur Canal+, Arthur Desmas a officialisé la fin définitive de sa carrière professionnelle à 32 ans. Le gardien de but doit renoncer au football sur ordre strict de son neurochirurgien en raison de commotions cérébrales à répétition.

C'est une issue brutale pour le gardien de but français. Libre de tout contrat après une dernière expérience sportive disputée au Qatar sous les couleurs d'Al-Duhail SC, Arthur Desmas a annoncé son retrait des terrains le mercredi 28 octobre 2026. L'ancien joueur du Havre AC présentait en effet des lésions persistantes qui ne montraient plus la moindre amélioration au fil des examens médicaux. « Ce n'est même pas moi qui prends la décision, c'est le neurochirurgien qui m'a dit : "Écoute, ça n'évolue pas, il va falloir que tu mettes un terme à ta carrière" », a-t-il raconté. Face à cette situation critique, le médecin lui a formellement imposé de raccrocher les gants pour préserver sa santé future. Un verdict sans appel. Formé au Stade Brestois avant de garder les cages de Niort, de Rodez, de Clermont puis du HAC, avec qui il a disputé 82 rencontres et remporté le trophée UNFP de meilleur gardien de Ligue 2 en 2023, le gardien doit désormais quitter le haut niveau.

Les chocs subis à la tête laissent des traces profondes dans la vie de tous les jours. Au quotidien, Arthur Desmas souffre ainsi de maux de tête réguliers, mais aussi de défaillances de la mémoire immédiate et de troubles prononcés de la concentration. Le calvaire physique ne s'arrête pas là : le joueur subit également de vives douleurs au niveau des cervicales ainsi que des troubles oculaires persistants. Le gardien a mesuré l'ampleur de ses séquelles lors d'une scène intime de sa vie de famille, lorsqu'il s'est retrouvé dans l'incapacité d'attraper une simple balle lancée par son propre fils. Cet événement marquant a confirmé la gravité de son état neurologique et la nécessité de stopper immédiatement toute pratique sportive professionnelle.

Au-delà de son cas personnel, Arthur Desmas entend désormais éveiller les consciences sur les traumatismes crâniens dans sa discipline. L'ancien Havrais appelle à briser le tabou qui entoure les commotions cérébrales dans le football. Il déplore que cette problématique majeure demeure largement sous-estimée et beaucoup moins médiatisée sur les pelouses de football que dans d'autres sports de contact, à l'image du rugby ou de la boxe, où les protocoles et la prévention sont plus visibles. Le portier de 32 ans espère ainsi que son témoignage permettra de faire évoluer la prise en charge des chocs à la tête chez les footballeurs.

#2413. « En face de moi, quelqu'un d'assez froid » : La surprenante réaction de Karim Benzema lors du coup de téléphone lui apprenant qu'il a gagné le Ballon d'Or

Couronné lors de la cérémonie du Ballon d'Or, Karim Benzema n'avait pourtant pas laissé éclater sa joie au moment d'apprendre la nouvelle par téléphone. L'ancien patron de France Football, Pascal Ferré, a dévoilé les coulisses de cet appel.

Le 17 octobre 2022, Karim Benzema recevait officiellement le 66e Ballon d'Or au Théâtre du Châtelet à Paris, venant ainsi concrétiser une saison exceptionnelle et plus largement un carrière au plus haut niveau. Pourtant, quelques jours avant la cérémonie, le rituel de l'annonce officielle a donné lieu à une scène particulièrement inattendue. Pascal Ferré, qui a dirigé la rédaction de France Football et l'organisation du trophée jusqu'à la fin de l'année 2022, a composé le numéro du buteur pour lui prononcer la nouvelle. À l'autre bout du combiné, la réaction du joueur a laissé le dirigeant perplexe.

Une retenue déconcertante. Alors que le Croate Luka Modrić avait par exemple fondu en larmes au téléphone lors de sa victoire en 2018, l'attaquant tricolore a réagi avec un détachement déroutant en lâchant un simple « Ah bon, d'accord, merci ».

Mais cette apparente froideur cachait en réalité une explication bien précise. Soumis à une obligation de confidentialité absolue sur le palmarès jusqu'à la remise officielle du trophée, Karim Benzema ne pouvait rien laisser paraître. Dans une vidéo diffusée par Le Vestiaire, Pascal Ferré a raconté cet échange et les explications données par Karim Benzema quelques jours plus tard.

Entouré de coéquipiers francophones, le futur lauréat risquait de trahir le secret au moindre mot d'enthousiasme. Karim Benzema a donc dû réprimer ses émotions devant ses partenaires avant de pouvoir enfin exprimer son immense joie une fois seul au volant de sa voiture.

Ces révélations figurent parmi les nombreuses anecdotes compilées dans le livre de Pascal Ferré intitulé La Face cachée du Ballon d'Or, paru en octobre 2026 aux éditions Albin Michel. Cet épisode témoigne de la gestion complexe du secret qui entoure traditionnellement la récompense. D'ailleurs, cette époque du coup de fil préalable au lauréat appartient désormais au passé.

Depuis l'édition 2024, les organisateurs de France Football ont décidé de bouleverser leurs habitudes en ne prévenant plus le vainqueur par téléphone avant la cérémonie. Un changement radical destiné à préserver le suspense jusqu'au direct de la remise du prix.

#2411. « Des premiers contacts ont été pris » : Un grand club italien pense à Didier Deschamps

En grande difficulté sur le plan sportif, la Juventus Turin songe sérieusement à changer d'entraîneur pour remplacer Luciano Spalletti. Libre depuis son départ des Bleus à l'été 2026, Didier Deschamps figure dans la short-list turinoise et se tiendrait prêt à faire son retour.

La crise couve du côté du Piémont. Mercredi 28 octobre 2026, la Juventus Turin s'est inclinée (2-0) face au Genoa lors de la 9e journée de Serie A, concédant des buts de Kingsley Ehizibue (12e) et Tommaso Baldanzi (28e) à Marassi. Cette troisième défaite de la saison en championnat place la formation turinoise à une décevante huitième place au classement. Le quotidien La Stampa s'est d'ailleurs montré impitoyable au lendemain du revers : « C'est une non-équipe, sans âme et sans idées, sans personnalité et sans qualité. »

Arrivé en octobre 2025 pour succéder à Igor Tudor, Luciano Spalletti voit sa position directement menacée par cette série négative. Bien que sous contrat jusqu'en 2028, le technicien toscan est désormais fragilisé par le manque d'idées de son équipe. Un constat alarmant.

Pour succéder à Luciano Spalletti, plusieurs profils circulent déjà. Les noms d'Antonio Conte et de Stefano Pioli sont notamment cités par la presse transalpine. Toutefois, selon La Repubblica, Conte ne serait pas particulièrement emballé à l'idée d'un retour et préférerait attendre une opportunité à Manchester United en cas d'éviction de Michael Carrick. Dès lors, le feuilleton prend une tout autre tournure avec la piste Didier Deschamps. Le quotidien La Stampa a ainsi révélé que des démarches concrètes avaient débuté : « Des premiers contacts ont également été pris (...) Il est libre et attend le bon projet pour rebondir, après quatorze années à la tête de l'équipe de France. Sa disponibilité a déjà été communiquée par des intermédiaires ».

Libre de tout engagement depuis l'été 2026, date à laquelle il a cédé sa place à Zinédine Zidane après quatorze années passées à la tête de l'équipe de France, Didier Deschamps a fait savoir par des intermédiaires qu'il était disponible pour revenir sur le banc piémontais. Sur le banc des Bleus, il a remporté la Coupe du monde 2018 et la Ligue des nations 2021, tout en atteignant les finales de l'Euro 2016 et du Mondial 2022. L'ancien sélectionneur tricolore connaît d'ailleurs intimement la maison bianconera. Didier Deschamps a porté les couleurs de la Juventus comme joueur entre 1994 et 1999, remportant notamment la Ligue des champions en 1996 et trois championnats d'Italie, avant d'entraîner l'équipe en Serie B lors de la saison 2006-2007 à la suite du Calciopoli. Un passé glorieux.

Le calendrier ne laisse aucun répit au club turinois. Luciano Spalletti pourrait en effet jouer son avenir lors de la réception du Napoli le dimanche 1er novembre 2026 à 11h45 à l'Allianz Stadium, à l'occasion de la 10e journée de Serie A.

La Juventus enchaînera ensuite par un déplacement sur la pelouse de l'AZ Alkmaar à l'AFAS Stadion, le jeudi 5 novembre 2026 à 12h00, en Ligue Europa.
